title: fix: record reported worker type at daemon registration
description: Daemon prerequisite split from task-bdf6db6f65b04a009c88c1e49aed3848; original task remains the launcher/integration gate with its DoD unchanged. Deliver optional workerType on claim_next_task and join_team, validate against existing WorkerType values CLAUDE/CODEX/GEMINI/GROK, and create/refresh worker.type rather than hardcoding CLAUDE. Normalize only by exact uppercase membership: missing, unknown or malformed input uses CLAUDE (no new rejection). Refresh an existing seat on valid claim invocations before normal alreadyAssigned/no-work/governor return paths, without changing assignment, attempt or presence rules; do not create a worker on an otherwise refused/empty claim just to refresh type. join_team must validate team/worker before changing state; rejoin updates type without resetting current task, status or membership. chat_who currently omits type: add type to every returned online entry (cursor, waiting, both), preserving fields/filtering; list_workers already projects w.type. Own claimNextTask.ts, joinTeam.ts, chatWho.ts, one new workerType.test.ts, docs/MCP_SERVER.md. No launchers, proxy, schema migration or global worker-store refactor. Keep duplication to the tiny allowlist rather than expanding the schema surface. Verification from repository root: (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test). Original final integration task re-runs daemon and proxy suites together.
definitionOfDone: claim_next_task and join_team expose optional workerType and table-driven tests persist CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI, GROK for newly registered seats.

Tests prove an existing seat refreshes type on claim/resume/no-work and rejoin; join preserves currentTaskId/status; missing/unknown/non-string values fall back to CLAUDE without failing solely on type.
Tests prove invalid team IDs and invalid claim statuses/runner identity retain existing failure/no-assignment behavior; a denied claim never creates a new worker merely for type.
list_workers and every chat_who source branch expose the persisted type, covered by mutation-resistant tests without changing presence/membership semantics.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md documents the optional field, fallback/refresh semantics and additive chat_who output; fresh (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test) exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
join_team + shared helpers (joinTeam.ts), test-first. Load test-driven-development: write the join cases in the new packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/workerType.test.ts, watch them fail, then implement.

(a) Export two helpers from joinTeam.ts; claimNextTask.ts imports them in step 2. One definition only: no runtime constant in types/schema.ts, no new util file.
- normalizeWorkerType(value: unknown): WorkerType. Returns the value only when it is a string that is EXACTLY one of CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI, GROK (case-sensitive). Build the allowlist as Record<WorkerType, true> so tsc fails if WorkerType ever grows, and test membership with Object.hasOwn so prototype names such as 'constructor' or 'toString' never match. Every other value ('codex', ' CODEX', '', 'OPENAI', null, 42, true, arrays, objects) returns 'CLAUDE'. Never throws: no new rejection.
- refreshWorkerType(state, workerId: string | undefined, reported: unknown): Promise<void>. No-op when workerId is falsy, when reported === undefined (the key was omitted = not reported, so an existing record keeps its type), or when no record exists (it never creates one). Otherwise normalize; if the result equals the stored type, do nothing: no disk write and no WORKER_UPDATED, because idle wrappers poll claim_next_task. Else call state.updateWorker(workerId, { type, lastActivityAt: worker.lastActivityAt }). Passing the stored lastActivityAt keeps a type change from counting as presence (updateWorker otherwise stamps now); status is untouched, so a DEAD record stays DEAD with its prune clock intact. For error handling, wrap the write in try/catch and logger.warn({ workerId, type, error }, ...) on failure. A failed type write never fails the calling tool: type is informational, and updateWorker writes disk before the map, so the old type stays consistent.

(b) join_team: add an optional workerType property to inputSchema.properties ({ type: 'string', description naming the four values, the CLAUDE fallback and that omitting it leaves an existing record's type alone }). Do NOT add it to required, and add no enum: an enum lets MCP clients refuse values the daemon must accept. Read it as unknown. Keep the existing order and add the type at two points:
1. required teamId/workerId;
2. the team must exist (an unknown team throws before ANY write, as today);
3. auto-register a missing record with type: normalizeWorkerType(params.workerType) (omitted gives CLAUDE);
4. addTeamMember (a full team still throws here; a record step 3 just created keeps its reported type, since the pre-existing auto-register-then-join order does not change);
5. revive a DEAD record to IDLE;
6. await refreshWorkerType(state, params.workerId, params.workerType) LAST, so only a successful join refreshes an existing record. It never touches currentTaskId, status, teamId, memberIds or chatCursors.
Mention the field in the tool description.

Tests (join part of workerType.test.ts). Use the ToolTestHarness pattern of joinTeam.notification.test.ts. afterEach runs vi.restoreAllMocks() then h.cleanup().
1. inputSchema.properties has workerType, and required does not include it.
2. it.each over the four names: a new seat joins with that value. Its in-memory record type AND the JSON at .moe/workers/<id>.json (fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse) both equal the value.
3. it.each fallback for a new seat, each giving CLAUDE with the join resolving to the team (no throw): omitted, 'codex', 'Codex', ' CODEX', '', 'OPENAI', 'constructor', null, 42, true, ['CODEX'], {}.
4. A busy existing member (status CODING, currentTaskId 'task-1', a chat cursor, already in the team) rejoins with 'GEMINI'. Type becomes GEMINI. Every other field, lastActivityAt included, equals the before-snapshot, and memberIds is unchanged (no duplicate).
5. An existing CODEX member rejoins with workerType omitted: the record toEqual the before-snapshot. This pins backward compatibility, and the landed joinTeam.notification.test.ts relies on it too; do not edit that file.
6. An existing CODEX member rejoins with 'aider': type becomes CLAUDE.
7. A DEAD seat (made DEAD with deregisterWorkerTool) rejoins with 'GROK': status IDLE, type GROK.
8. Refusals, each with workerType 'GROK':
- an unknown teamId for an unknown seat throws, and no record or file exists afterwards;
- an unknown teamId for an existing CODEX seat throws, and its type stays CODEX;
- a full team (maxSize 1, already occupied) for an existing CODEX seat throws 'is full', and its type stays CODEX.
9. Error handling: vi.spyOn(h.state, 'updateWorker').mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('EBUSY')) during an existing member's type-only rejoin. The join still resolves with the team, and the type is unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
claim_next_task (claimNextTask.ts), test-first, importing normalizeWorkerType/refreshWorkerType from './joinTeam.js'.

(a) Add an optional workerType to inputSchema.properties (string; same description as join_team; no enum; not required). Add workerType?: unknown to the params cast.

(b) Refresh only after input validation, and before every return path:
- These validations come first, unchanged: empty statuses (MISSING_REQUIRED), readProcessIdentity (a malformed or half runner identity gives INVALID_INPUT), and an unloaded project. A claim refused by any of them writes nothing.
- Governor redirect: inside the resolveWorkerRole(...) === 'governor' branch, which today answers BEFORE the claimable-status check, first await refreshWorkerType(state, params.workerId, params.workerType), then return the existing enter_governance nudge unchanged.
- Every other caller: right after assertAgentClaimableStatuses(statuses), so BACKLOG/DONE/BLOCKED statuses throw first and refresh nothing, add await refreshWorkerType(state, params.workerId, params.workerType). It sits before blockingHold, the finalizing hold, the explicit-taskId checks, the ranked pool, the no-work return and the candidate loop. That covers alreadyAssigned (the wrapper's resume relaunch), no work, an explicit resume, and a claim refused later for a non-input reason. Because the helper never creates a record, an unknown seat whose claim ends without an assignment still has no record.

(c) Success path: in the createWorker branch, replace the hardcoded const workerType: WorkerType = 'CLAUDE' with normalizeWorkerType(params.workerType) (omitted gives CLAUDE). Leave the existing-record update branch alone: the up-front refresh already recorded the type, DEAD records included. Do not change ranking, eviction, attempt open/adopt, healTeamMembership, the '<id> is online' post or any response shape. Drop the WorkerType import only if nothing uses it any more.

Tests (claim part of workerType.test.ts). Each it.each row needs its own fresh harness (beforeEach h.init/setupMoeFolder), because claim_next_task refuses a second solo seat on the same epic+status. Write epic-1 and a PLANNING task-1, then await h.state.load(). Call claimNextTaskTool(h.state).handler({ statuses: ['PLANNING'], workerId, workerType, ... }, h.state).
1. inputSchema exposes workerType, and it is not required.
2. it.each over the four names: a new seat claims, gets hasNext true, and its record type and disk JSON equal the value. Fallback rows (omitted, 'grok', 'UNKNOWN', null, 7) give CLAUDE and still hasNext true.
3. An existing IDLE CLAUDE seat claims with 'GEMINI': task-1 is assigned to it and its type is GEMINI.
4. Resume. A seat claims task-1 with 'CODEX'; keep attemptId and generation.
- An explicit re-claim { taskId: 'task-1', workerType: 'GROK' } gives hasNext true, the SAME attemptId and generation, assignedWorkerId unchanged, and type GROK.
- A ranked re-claim with 'CODEX' gives alreadyAssigned.taskId 'task-1' and type CODEX, and listAttempts(h.state, 'task-1') toEqual the previous list.
5. No work (no claimable task): an existing seat claims with 'CODEX'. Expect hasNext false, nextAction.tool 'moe.wait_for_task', and type CODEX. Status, currentTaskId, epicId, teamId and lastActivityAt equal the before-snapshot: no presence change.
6. Governor: a registered 'governor-<x>' seat (role from the id prefix) claims with 'CODEX'. Expect nextAction.tool 'moe.enter_governance', type CODEX, and no task assigned.
7. workerType omitted on an existing CODEX seat (both a successful claim and a no-work claim): the type stays CODEX. A no-work claim reporting the type the record already has leaves updateWorker uncalled (spy).
8. Invalid invocations write nothing. Run each with workerType 'GROK', for an existing CODEX seat and for an unknown seat:
- statuses [] gives MISSING_REQUIRED;
- ['BACKLOG'] gives INVALID_INPUT;
- processStartedAt without host gives INVALID_INPUT;
- a blank host gives INVALID_INPUT.
Assert the codeName. The existing seat stays CODEX, the unknown seat has no record and no file, and nothing is assigned.
9. A denied claim never creates a record. Use an unknown seat with 'GEMINI' in each case:
- (i) the board has no claimable task;
- (ii) an explicit taskId is assigned to another live seat, which throws NOT_ALLOWED;
- (iii) another live seat holds a PLANNING task in epic-1 and a second PLANNING task is free, so the epic+status rule refuses the solo seat.
In each case the seat has no record and no file, and every task assignment is unchanged.
10. The error handling path: updateWorker is rejected once during a type-only refresh on a no-work claim. The claim still answers hasNext false, and the type is unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
chat_who projection (chatWho.ts) + list_workers proof.

Add type: worker.type to all three online.push sites (channel-filtered cursor, unfiltered, and waiting), and add type to the online element's declared shape. The 'both' upgrade reuses the cursor entry, so it carries type too. Do not change the 120s presence window, the filters, the seen map, ordering or any other field. listWorkers.ts already projects w.type, so leave it unchanged.

Tests (workerType.test.ts):
1. chat_who with channel 'chan-x'. Seats:
- a CODEX seat with chatCursors['chan-x'] and fresh lastActivityAt: source 'cursor';
- a GEMINI seat with no cursor but in activeChatWaiters watching chan-x: 'waiting';
- a GROK seat with a cursor that is also waiting: 'both';
- a CLAUDE seat whose waiter has channels null (watches every channel): 'waiting'.
These must be absent: a stale seat (lastActivityAt 10 minutes old) with a cursor; a fresh seat with neither a cursor nor a waiter; a waiter on another channel only.
Assert online, sorted by workerId, toEqual the full objects { workerId, type, status, lastActivity, currentTaskId, source }. Then dropping type from any one branch, or any presence or membership drift, fails the test.
2. chat_who without a channel: every fresh seat appears exactly once with source 'cursor' and its type. The stale seat is absent.
3. list_workers: seats registered through join_team and claim_next_task with each of the four names report that type. After a rejoin with a new value, list_workers shows the new one.

Waiters: activeChatWaiters.set(id, { resolve: () => {}, unsubscribe: () => {}, timer: setTimeout(() => {}, 60_000), channels: new Set(['chan-x']) or null }). afterEach clears every waiter's timer and then the map, as the WebSocketServer tests do, so a failing test leaks nothing into other files. Sort before comparing, because state.workers follows directory-listing order, which differs by OS.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Choices made, with the rejected alternatives:
1. An omitted workerType never resets an existing record. It is not reported, so a new record gets CLAUDE and an existing one keeps its type. Resetting it to CLAUDE was rejected for three reasons:
- a non-reporting caller (the IDE board, scripts/moe-call.sh, an older proxy or wrapper) would overwrite a type that a launcher seat reported;
- it would add a disk write and a WORKER_UPDATED on every idle claim poll;
- the landed joinTeam.notification.test.ts pins a CODEX member's omitted-type rejoin as byte-identical.
Any supplied value (task-eb85340b's proxy forwards non-blank strings verbatim) is normalized by exact membership, and everything else becomes CLAUDE. This is how DoD 2's 'missing ... falls back to CLAUDE' is read: at registration.
2. No enum in either inputSchema, because an enum would let MCP clients refuse values the daemon must accept. That would be a new rejection, which the task forbids.
3. The allowlist lives in joinTeam.ts (exported, imported by claim), not in types/schema.ts and not in a new util. The task caps the owned files and asks for no schema surface. Record<WorkerType, true> keeps it exhaustive at compile time.
4. Refreshing only in the claim success path was rejected: alreadyAssigned, no-work and the governor redirect never reach it.
5. DEAD records are not special-cased. A refresh keeps status and lastActivityAt, so it changes no presence or prune clock. join_team revives a DEAD record before it refreshes.
6. A failed type write logs and continues, because the field is informational. Creation and assignment errors still propagate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Behavior the plan relies on:
- McpAdapter does not validate arguments against inputSchema; the handlers read raw args.
- updateWorker (state/workerStore.ts) stamps lastActivityAt=now unless the update passes one. A DEAD record emits WORKER_DELETED instead of WORKER_UPDATED. touchWorker refuses DEAD records.
- The claim handler runs inside state.runExclusive. Its order: statuses non-empty, readProcessIdentity, project loaded, governor redirect (registered seat, resolveWorkerRole via team role then the id prefix 'governor-'), assertAgentClaimableStatuses, blockingHold (a ranked claim by a seat holding a task gets alreadyAssigned; an explicit taskId of the held task is the resume, which adopts the open attempt), the finalizing hold, explicit-taskId checks or the ranked pool, the no-work return, then the candidate loop. A worker record is created only after the assignment write (createWorker type hardcoded CLAUDE at about line 650).
- joinTeam auto-registers before addTeamMember, which throws 'Team ... is full' after that create. createWorker logs WORKER_CREATED { workerId, type }.
- chatWho has three push sites plus the 'both' upgrade, and no tests other than the registry name. listWorkers already returns type. Nothing outside the daemon parses chat_who output (scripts, plugins and proxy were grepped).
- getWorker reads the in-memory map only. tsconfig excludes *.test.ts.
- The harness writes .moe/workers/<id>.json. enterGovernance.ts:91 still auto-creates CLAUDE; that is out of scope, because governor seats register through their pre-flight join_team.
